explanations: In Logger.child, Object.assign(this.bindings, fields) mutates the parent's bindings object instead of copying it. Every child call writes requestId, userId, tripId and supplier into the root logger's shared bindings, so the root logger and all existing children share one object. Under concurrent bookings, a log line from request A can carry request B's requestId and userId (whichever child was created last), making logs misattributed and impossible to correlate. The fix is to merge into a fresh object: { ...this.bindings, ...fields }.

error() builds errFields with error.type, error.message and error.stack for Error instances and spreads both errFields and fields into the record, and log() also spreads this.bindings. Fields are merged, not replaced; String(err) is only used for non-Error values; there is no "err" key holding the raw Error.

In log(), the record literal lists ts, level and msg first and spreads bindings and fields afterwards, so a later key with the same name wins: level becomes "vip". Object spread never renames keys, and the level filter runs on the method's level argument, not on fields.

process.env.LOG_LEVEL is undefined, so ?? falls back to "info". info (20) and error (40) are at or above the threshold, so started, confirmed and failed are all written; only debug would be filtered. It is not undefined, not unfiltered, and info events are not suppressed.
